ext::http_batch.note: One generic one-thread/PollSet engine owns canonical HTTP preparation, admission, refill, accounting and input-order partial results. run_with_until accepts typed Factory/Driver/error parameters; run_until supplies the plain adapter. Report/Failure.destroy require Destroy<E>; take transfers cleanup authority. before_wait Ok(true) preserves observed Interest and descriptor identity through registration. Borrowed E backing outlives final Report/taken-outcome use and destruction, including after run return. Current plain execution passes eight groups and 103 cases through two receipts: seven original groups/102 cases in 13.00 seconds and one causal wait-retirement case in 10.07 seconds. The first retirement fixture failed under incoherent validation/work caps; coherent caps preserve its original allowance and causal assertions, and the retry passes without a product accounting change. All six connected HTTPS groups separately pass 108 cases. Historical 480432e8 receipts retain separate scope; current fetch-many also passes all five application groups in 24.18 seconds, including all 59 reached allocation failures and a 64-job/four-socket control. Logical retention/work caps exclude allocator capacities, temporary candidates, native transport storage/CPU and RSS. Worker threads remain separate work.

declarations.run_with_until: Shared scheduler over typed jobs, Factory and Driver; begin consumes canonical Prepared on every result. Job/factory backing stays borrowed through return; borrowed E backing additionally survives final Report/taken-outcome use and destruction. before_wait Ok(true) preserves interest/descriptor identity through registration. Current plain eight-group/103-case and HTTPS six-group/108-case receipts are separate.
declarations.run_until: Plain HTTP adapter over the same generic engine, returning Report<http_client::Failure> and Failure<http_client::Failure>. All eight current plain groups pass 103 cases across two native Linux x86_64 receipts.

ext::http_client.note: Prepared canonically validates and copies request backing without sockets. into_protocol transfers it to the transport-free Protocol; begin supplies the plain socket driver. Protocol centralizes framing, encoding, decoding, confirmed progress, limits and Response transfer. Trailing selects default Discard or explicit Reject for already-received surplus; neither waits for future bytes. Plain steps never poll and offer at most 1024 bytes per active network leaf. Current direct Protocol execution passes one state/ownership group in 7.94 seconds with 247 explicitly balanced successful mappings and zero network calls, not 247 allocation-denial tests. The refactored synchronous client passes all six groups/188 cases in 27.70 seconds; direct Exchange passes five groups/83 cases through separate 7.93- and 9.90-second receipts with unchanged production source. Historical 480432e8 receipts remain separate. TLS stays in its adapter and OpenSSL; other targets remain unverified.

declarations.prepare_until: Canonical request preflight and owned staging without sockets; successful Prepared owners must be consumed with begin or destroyed.
declarations.begin_until: Preparation followed by consuming Prepared.begin; socket opening only, with connect and HTTP progress performed by Exchange.step.
declarations.exchange_until: Synchronous driver over the shared Prepared/Exchange engine, charging poll participation against the same cumulative deadline and quotas.

ext::https_batch.note: Thin verified HTTPS factory/driver adapter over the single generic HTTP batch engine. Jobs borrow numeric endpoints, certificate identities and HTTP Requests; job/context backing remains unchanged through return. All HTTP requests prepare before sockets; per-job TLS option/identity admission and native verification occur later. Typed results preserve complete HTTPS diagnostics, input order, response ownership and partial outcomes. OpenSSL performs TLS and cryptography; callers establish SIGPIPE policy, and TLS 1.2/1.3 retry/closure scope follows https_client. All six connected groups pass 108 cases through three Linux x86_64/glibc/OpenSSL 3 receipts, including 42 reached source-allocation failures and six direct-step/abort controls. Plain batch separately passes eight groups/103 cases. The migrated HTTPS fetch passes four app groups/63 cases, and mutual-TLS application modes pass three groups/101 cases excluding prepared-context streams. Historical and current receipt scopes remain distinct; worker/server orchestration remains open.

declarations.run_until: Runs verified HTTPS jobs through http_batch.run_with_until with typed https_client::Failure outcomes, one shared Context/deadline and explicit HTTP/TLS/scheduler budgets. Six focused groups pass 108 cases on Linux x86_64; application and plain-batch receipts have separate scopes.

ext::https_client.note: Resumable numeric TCP/OpenSSL transport for the shared HTTP Protocol, without a second HTTP parser. Begin consumes Prepared on every result, retaining an independent native Context reference and copying identity bytes before one nonblocking socket opens. Steps never poll; TLS uses stable staged writes, independent readiness needs and explicit TLS-call/I/O/deadline budgets. Early-final closure distinguishes TLS 1.3 notification from TLS 1.2 deferral; authenticated EOF is required for close-delimited bodies. Typed metadata preserves HTTP/TLS/cleanup diagnostics. Six connected HTTPS groups pass 108 cases across three native Linux x86_64/glibc/OpenSSL 3 receipts, including 42 reached source-allocation failures and six direct-step/abort controls. The migrated HTTPS app separately passes four groups/63 cases, and affected mutual-TLS app modes pass three groups/101 cases excluding prepared-context streams. These finite receipts do not establish every TLS schedule or another target. A confirmed 14-line nested enum-pattern reduction rejects with LNC0006; its explicit two-match x86_64 control executes all four assertions. No compiler or production transport change was needed for that expression spelling.

declarations.begin_with_context_until: Consumes and disarms canonical Prepared, preserving its deadline and charged HTTP state. Retains an independent native Context reference and identity copy; successful begin owns the transport until terminal cleanup.
declarations.exchange_until: Synchronous facade over the same resumable verified Exchange and canonical HTTP Protocol; caller trust, identity, SIGPIPE policy and absolute deadline remain explicit.

ext::lexer.note: Ordered UTF-8 token rules reuse the canonical regex engine's anchored longest-prefix search. The longest byte span wins, with declaration order resolving ties; skip rules consume input and empty winners or unmatched input are terminal errors. Cursors borrow the compiled Lexer and validated immutable input, and tokens borrow input bytes. Construction, input, step, token, search-call and reserved VM-allowance limits are explicit; the guides define allocation costs, work-counter scope and the current execution evidence.

ext::openssl_digest.note: Digests execute through OpenSSL 3 EVP on Linux x86_64/glibc with checked native C linking and an explicit libcrypto dependency. The raw extern declarations require caller-managed native pointer and lifetime contracts.

ext::openssl_tls.note: Client, server and mutual TLS delegate to OpenSSL 3 libssl/libcrypto on Linux x86_64/glibc. Mandatory client-side server chain/DNS/IP verification and explicit server required-peer policy do not assign application authorization. Manual sessions borrow connected nonblocking sockets and require caller deadlines/SIGPIPE policy. Current independent read/write readiness, stable staged retries, permitted duplex interleaving, read quiescence, local shutdown, version diagnostics and Context retention pass nine new duplex groups/36 cases, including all five reached source-allocation failures. Selected legacy client/server/mutual-TLS retry guards separately pass 3, 1 and 6 cases; these are not full reruns of all historical TLS suites. Current connected HTTPS and migrated application receipts have separate scope. Native crypto CPU/storage costs are outside logical HTTP quotas.

ext::regex.note: The read-only search_work_limit accessor exposes the existing per-search VM allowance for aggregate adapters. Validated Input and anchored longest-prefix methods reuse the existing ordered Pike engine while preserving full-input assertions and capture priority on equal endpoints; ordinary find and Matches retain leftmost-first behavior. The lexer guide defines endpoint selection and borrowed input lifetime. Bounded split/replacement continue to reuse the canonical Matches cursor.

std::command.note: Process-group creation is explicit. Group signaling requires the confirmed original group and an owned, unreaped leader; non-reaping terminal observations do not consume that anchor. Final reaping or lost-child evidence revokes it. std::command_capture.note: Progress.status may be an observed terminal status while Progress.reaped is false. Capture retains the unreaped leader anchor while draining acquired pipes, then performs a charged final nonblocking reap before success. A failure can retain that Child authority unless ownership was lost or final reaping already occurred; captured output owners and child cleanup remain explicit. The guides define operation/deadline scope and current execution evidence.

std::command_raw.note: Internal Linux syscall support for std::command, including process-group setup and non-reaping exit observation.
